items.title: docs: health.md says a running CronJob is Progressing, but the built-in check returns Healthy
items.body:
Checklist:

- [x] I've searched in the docs and FAQ for my answer: https://bit.ly/argocd-faq.
- [x] I've included steps to reproduce the bug.
- [x] I've pasted the output of `argocd version`.

**Describe the bug**

This is a documentation bug. The CronJob section of the [Resource Health](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/latest/operator-manual/health/#cronjob) page says:

> If the last scheduled job for this CronJob is running, the CronJob will be marked as "Progressing"

The built-in check in `resource_customizations/batch/CronJob/health.lua` never returns "Progressing". It returns "Healthy" while a job is running, before the first successful run, and when the CronJob is suspended. It returns "Degraded" only when the last run failed and nothing is running. The [3.1 to 3.2 upgrade notes](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/latest/operator-manual/upgrading/3.1-3.2/#cronjob-health) already describe this, but the health page was not updated, so readers expect a state that never appears.

**To Reproduce**

1. Deploy an Application that contains a CronJob whose job runs for a few minutes.
2. While the job runs, look at the CronJob health in the UI or with `argocd app get`.
3. The CronJob shows "Healthy", not "Progressing" as the docs say.

**Expected behavior**

The health page describes what the built-in check returns, and lists the ways to keep a CronJob out of the Application health (`argocd.argoproj.io/ignore-healthcheck` annotation, or a `resource.customizations.health.batch_CronJob` override). I have a small docs-only change ready and can open a PR if this is accepted.

Related: #24429, #24428 (behavior discussions; this issue is only about the docs matching current behavior).

**Version**

Observed on v3.5.1 (`quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v3.5.1`); the docs text is the same on master.

**Logs**

Not applicable.
